strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain role of a kitchen garden in food and nutrition security b) describe innovative technologies for kitchen gardening c) classify food crops suitable for growing in a kitchen garden d) establish a kitchen garden for provision of healthy and affordable food e) adopt innovative technologies in kitchen gardening for food and nutrition security.

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) describe methods of heat transfer when cooking foods b) classify carbohydrate foods found in different localities c) explain the effect of heat on starchy carbohydrate foods d) practise ways to conserve food nutrients when cooking carbohydrate foods e) Outline safety measures to observe in preparing and cooking carbohydrates f) appreciate the importance of heat in making carbohydrate foods palatable and nutritious.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • search and brainstorm on the meaning and methods of heat transfer when cooking foods (radiation, conduction and convection) • use digital devices, print material, to search, brainstorm and classify different carbohydrate foods found in the localities (starchy foods, simple and double sugars). Present findings during class plenary, • carry out experiments to investigate and record effects of heat on starchy carbohydrate foods in relation to taste, aroma, texture, colour and consistency for liquid foods  brainstorm effect of moist heat (gelatinisation) and dry
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is it advisable to cook starchy carbohydrate foods before consumption? 2. How are starchy carbohydrate foods cooked at home?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain factors to consider during table setting in meal presentation b) describe requirements for table setting when serving meals c) set a table for a meal presentation d) prepare and present a simple lunch using the various styles of meal service e) appreciate importance of table setting in meal presentation.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to : • brainstorm on the meaning and importance of meal presentation.  study, reflect and brainstorm on the factors considered during table setting using reference books, digital devices, share personal experiences, resources persons, present findings in class,  identify the requirements such as table, table linen (table cloth, napkins, place mats) centre piece, dinner and side plates, cutlery (table fork, spoon, knife), water glass used in table setting,  watch a demonstration or a video clip showing placement of requirements during table setting and set a cover for a main meal (taking appropriate action in response to global public health concerns),
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Which factors determine how a table should be set? 2. Why is it important to observe table etiquette during meals?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) outline guidelines to consider when planning meals for different special groups b) analyse feeding habits and food taboos for the special groups c) plan meals for different special groups, d) prepare and present meals for special groups, e) recognise the importance of planning meals for different special groups.
strands.experiences: Learner will be guided to: • research on special groups and their food requirements. Present findings in class, • using digital materials, reference books, personal experiences, resource person explore simple guidelines to consider when choosing meals for different special groups (infants/babies, children, adolescents, older persons, manual workers, invalids, vegetarians, convalescents, expectant mother and lactating mothers) • engage a resource person to brainstorm on different feeding habits and taboos for special groups ( expectant and lactating mothers, adolescents, small and older children, older persons) • in groups and using digital planner, recipe books, reference books, e-pubs, video clips, resource persons practise simple meal planning skills for different special groups
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do some people take special diets? 2. How do food taboos and superstitions affect choice of meals for special groups?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) explain factors to consider when planning meals for special occasions, b) describe guidelines to consider when planning meals for special occasions c) plan a meal for a special occasion d) present a food item or dish for a special occasion, e) appreciate the importance of planning meals for special occasion.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • examine, reflect and discuss as a class mistakes made while planning meals for special occasions, • brainstorm on factors to consider when planning meals for special occasions (funeral, birthday, wedding, graduation, initiation,) • in groups share experiences on successes and mistakes made while planning meals for special occasions, • study and share findings on guidelines to bear in mind while planning meals for special occasion., • plan suitable meals for special occasions( funeral, birthday, wedding, graduation, initiation) using recipe books, reference books, digital devices and resource persons • plan, prepare, cook and present food items or dishes for a special occasion using realia, recipe books, reference books, digital content.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why are some occasions considered special? 2. Which food items or dishes do you consider special and why?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) explain role of consumer awareness in consumer education b) examine consumer behaviour in satisfaction of household needs and wants c) evaluate types of consumer buyers in the market d) examine roles of a consumer in acquisition of goods and services, e) appreciate concept of consumer awareness for wise choices.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • explore and brainstorm on the meaning and importance of consumer awareness and present during class plenary, • share experiences on consumer behaviour when selecting, buying, using and disposing goods to satisfy needs and wants, • organise a role play or drama on the types of buyers and their characteristics (loyal customers, impulse shoppers, wandering consumers, need-based customers, discount customers), • engage actively with a resource person to discuss on the roles of a consumer in wise buying such as a decision maker, influencer,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How does consumers’ awareness influence behaviour when buying goods and services? 2. Why should consumers make wise choices when acquiring goods and services?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) examine concept of market competition in relation to the consumer b) explain the role of competition in the market place. c) assess factors that influence competition in the market. d) highlight fair and unfair market competition in acquisition of necessities for household use. e) describe benefits of unfair and fair competition in the consumer market. f) appreciate benefits of competition in the market in the acquisition of goods and services for household use.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • search using digital material, print materials or resource persons the meaning of the terms: market, market competition and competitor in relation to consumerism. Share with during class plenary, • brainstorm the reasons for the need for competition. In the market • research and brainstorm the reasons for competition in the market. Make a presentation on (price,quality , variety and innovation ,promotion), • Design and display messages and posters drawing on fair and unfair competition of a product, • Discuss the benefits and cons competition.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How does market competition ensure that the consumer gets value for their money? 2. What happens when markets lack competition?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) classify textile fibres based on their artificial sources. b) describe the properties of artificial fibres, c) describe uses of different artificial textile fibres d) carry out identification tests on artificial textile fibres e) appreciate various artificial textile fibres in clothing and household articles
strands.experiences: Learners will be guide to: • revise and discuss on Grade 7 on natural textiles fibres • draw a textile tree or flow chart to organise the various textile fibres based on their sources to include synthetic fibres (nylon, polyester and acrylic) and regenerated fibres (viscose rayon and acetate rayon), • collect and mount samples of fabrics made of artificial textile fibres in a sampler album, scrapbook or portfolio to show their properties, • use digital media to search and watch video clips on various uses of artificial textile fibres and present their findings in class plenary,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why are synthetic fibres more popular than natural fibres? 2. How would you differentiate nylon from acrylic fabrics?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) classify different types of seams used in clothing construction b) analyse factors to consider when choosing seams used in clothing construction c) examine qualities of well-made seams used in clothing construction d) make different seams used in clothing construction e) construct a simple garment using suitable seams f) value use of seams in clothing construction
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • revise on Grade 7 work on seams • build on Grade 7 strand on seams and search for more information on classification of seams used for making clothes and household articles, (conspicuous-overlaid (lapped seam) and machine-fell seam(double stitched) and inconspicuous- french seam,and plain and open seams done earlier in Grade 7)) • in groups research on, discuss and compile factors to consider when choosing different types of seams used to make clothes and household articles such as texture and weight of fabric, design and use of garment, position of seam, desired effect),
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is the plain and open seam methods popular in making clothes and household articles ? 2. How do you strengthen a seam?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe reasons for controlling fullness when making clothes and household articles, b) outline factors to consider when choosing methods of controlling fullness c) describe procedures for controlling fullness used when making clothes and household articles, d) make samples of different methods used to control fullness e) appreciate control of fullness in garment construction
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • research on and discuss the meaning of control of fullness. • reflect and brainstorm in pairs, on the reasons for controlling fullness when making clothes and household articles and present their findings in class, • search for information digital content, print material, resource persons and brainstorm on the factors to consider when choosing methods of controlling fullness (darts, pleats, tucks, gathers and easing) used in making clothes and household articles, • watch a demonstration and write the procedures for controlling fullness darts (single and double), pleats (inverted and box), tucks (plain and decorative), gathers and easing) used when making clothes and household articles
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How is fullness controlled in garment making? 2. What are the reasons for arranging fullness on a garment?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe human development from conception to birth. b) explain needs of an expectant mother, c) analyse preparations made for the baby’s arrival, d) investigate traditional beliefs and taboos associated with pregnancy and child birth, e) describe the choice and care for baby’s layette f) appreciate preparations made for baby’s arrival. . .
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • examine, reflect and brainstorm on conception (safe parenthood, foetal development) and signs of pregnancy in a human( positive and danger sign). Present in class plenary, • interact with digital devices and print materials and use research to explain the needs of an expectant mother such as proper dressing, diet, physical exercise and rest, personal hygiene, family and societal support, knowledge on maternity and paternity care, clinic attendance, needs of an expectant father ( Psychological, preparations, support, financial, information) • watch a video or a demonstration on preparations made for baby’s arrival such as layette, feeding equipment, bathing items,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can a mother-to -be make unborn baby comfortable in the womb? 2. Why is the role of a father-to- be important during pregnancy and after child birth?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand , the learner should be able to: a) outline factors to consider when choosing different methods of providing family shelter b) explain the advantages and disadvantages of different methods of providing family shelter, c) model different types of houses use to provide family shelter d) explain advantages and disadvantages of types of houses used in providing family shelter, e) appreciate the observance of human rights in providing family shelter for self and others. f) relate the human rights to providing family shelter. g) promote proper and safe family shelter in their locality.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • research on the meaning of family shelter • study and search using digital devices and print materials on the factors to consider when choosing different methods of providing family shelter. (renting, buying and building). Compare your findings with peers, • discuss in groups research and present findings on the advantages and disadvantages of the different methods of providing family shelter (renting, buying and building) • brainstorm and categorise family shelter (Type (modern or traditional), design (bungalow, maisonette, flats), and model the different types of house designs(room layout/orientation) and (materials used for construction). using realia,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can we improve housing the family? 2. What causes poor or bad housing?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) explain functions of different rooms or areas found in a family house or home b) illustrate room or area interrelationship in a family house or home c) outline factors that influence room or area interrelationship and placement in a family house or home d) appreciate the importance of understanding room interrelationship in house designs.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guide to: • use charts, pictures, digital material, reference books, and personal experiences to identify, justify and record functions of different types of rooms or areas found in a family house, then present their findings in class, • sketch a simple plan of a family house or home (sitting area/living, kitchen/cooking area, bathroom/bath shelter, toilet/latrine, bedroom/sleeping area, dining room/eating area, food store/storage area), • use their personal and cultural experiences, study pictures in books and on-line to generate,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do family houses have different rooms? 2. How are different rooms in a family house interrelated?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe types of kitchen plans in a home b) outline advantages and disadvantages of different kitchen plans c) explain factors that influence placement of working areas or centres in a kitchen plan d) sketch different kitchen plans in a family house e) appreciate placement of work centres in a kitchen plan.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • describe the kitchen areas in a house • using digital or print materials and personal experiences to study and brainstorm work centre and work triangle in a types of kitchen plans, • illustrate work centres and work triangle by use of sketches such as painted images or pictures of drawings, • Research and discuss factors that influence placement of working areas or centres in kitchen plans and share in class, • observe pictures, drawings or images of different types of kitchen plans ( one-wall, L-shaped, U-shaped, Island), corridor reflect, identify and share the observations with their peers in class, • Organise a debate on advantages and disadvantages of different kitchen plans in a family house,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why do people cook their food outside the kitchen? 2. Why should a kitchen be planned well before construction?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) describe methods of removing dirt from the kitchen surfaces b) explain procedures in daily, weekly and special cleaning carried out in the kitchen, c) carry out cleaning of the kitchen. d) appreciate a clean kitchen for healthy living.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • examine and brainstorm on the meaning of the following terms: loose dirt, fixed dirt found in the kitchen • research and brainstorm on methods of removing types of dirt from kitchen surfaces such as sweeping, dusting, wiping, mopping, vacuum cleaning, • discuss reasons for cleaning the kitchen (daily, weekly and special cleaning) • in groups brainstorm and make summaries on procedures used in daily, weekly and special cleaning of kitchen surfaces(walls, ceiling, floor, worktops) • clean (daily, weekly and special) the kitchen surfaces according to type such as earthen ware, cemented, wooden, tiled, terrazzo.
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. Why is it important to clean the kitchen? 2. . How is the kitchen kept clean for healthy living?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) examine meaning of terms related to colour, b) explain factors to consider when choosing a colour for home decoration, c) describe colour combinations for interior design and decoration, d) use colour to demonstrate colour scheme for various rooms in a family house e) appreciate harmony in the use of colour in the home.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • study and brainstorm on the meaning of terms related to colour (tint, shade, value, intensity, tone, hue).Write them down and add to the vocabulary class corner tint, shade, value, intensity, tone, hue), • Share experiences and discuss the factors considered when choosing colours for home decoration, • use digital and print resources to identify and interpret colour combination- colour wheel (primary, secondary and tertiary) • use digital illustrations, colour scheme (monochromatic, analogous complimentary) for interior design and decoration,
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can one make the paint colours flow in a family house? 2. What colours make a room bigger or smaller?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to: a) examine different soft furnishings used in the home b) examine factors to consider when choosing soft furnishings used in the home, c) explain the functions of soft furnishings in the home, d) make a soft furnishing item used in the home e) care for various soft furnishings in the home, f) appreciate the use of soft furnishings at home.
strands.experiences: Learners will be guided to: • in groups, brainstorm on the meaning of soft furnishings • list various soft furnishings used in the home using realia, digital devices , personal experiences, pictures and print materials, • research on the factors to consider when choosing soft furnishings in the home using digital devices, personal experiences and print materials and report their findings in class, • watch a video or a demonstration on how to make a soft furnishing item. • make a soft furnishing item with emphasize on choice of colour, skills of making, utility
strands.inquiryQuestions: 1. How can one make soft furnishings for use at home using local and safe resources? 2. Why are soft furnishings vital in a house?
